description: Choose a POS by business type: compare retail inventory, restaurant service, mobile selling and appointment workflows, then check the full cost and hardware.
aeo_answer: Choose a POS around the work your business does. Our shortlist starts with Square for straightforward retail or mobile selling, Shopify POS for a Shopify store selling in person, Toast for restaurant workflows, and Vagaro for appointment-based services. Compare Lightspeed when inventory requirements are more complex. Verify the plan, hardware and payment terms before choosing.

faq_json.question: Is free POS software the lowest-cost option?
faq_json.answer: Not necessarily. Add processing, hardware, paid features and the cost of operating the system. For low-value transactions, a fixed transaction charge can matter as much as the percentage rate.

faq_json.question: Can I use my existing phone or tablet?
faq_json.answer: Check the provider’s supported device, operating-system and reader list before purchasing. A compatible app does not mean every reader, printer or payment method will work with your device.

faq_json.question: What should I test in a POS demonstration?
faq_json.answer: Run a normal sale, a return and the hardest task in your business: a stock transfer, split restaurant check or rescheduled appointment. Then check the end-of-day report and the account receiving the deposit.

sources_json.name: Square POS demo and US fees

body_html:
The right POS is the one your staff can use for your actual sales, returns and end-of-day work. The recommendations below are an editorial shortlist based on provider documentation checked September 10, 2026. They are not a claim of hands-on testing or a universal ranking.

General retail and mobile selling: start with Square

Square’s POS demo covers sales, inventory, customers and refunds. Its published US entry-level in-person rate is 2.6% + $0.15, with no monthly software fee for that plan. Hardware and optional services can add cost. We would start here when the priority is a straightforward checkout with a relatively simple product catalog.

Before buying a mobile setup, check your exact phone, operating system and reader combination. Ask how the device handles a lost connection and what conditions apply to delayed card processing. Do not assume that every device or payment type has identical offline support. Compare the mobile payment options against your expected selling location.

A Shopify store selling in person: compare Shopify POS

Shopify POS brings in-person selling into the Shopify commerce system. It belongs on the shortlist when your online store and physical stock need to be managed together. Check which inventory, staff and location features require a higher POS plan rather than assuming they are included in your online-store subscription.

Use a real product with sizes or colors in the demonstration. Sell it online, collect it in store, return it and transfer the replacement to another location. Confirm that stock counts and customer records remain usable at each step.

Restaurants and cafes: compare Toast around service flow

Toast’s plans are built around restaurant operations. Our reason to shortlist it is the service workflow: taking an order, routing it to the kitchen, splitting the check and closing the shift. Compare the quote’s hardware, payment-processing agreement and add-ons as a package.

A cafe serving a short menu has different needs from a full-service restaurant. Ask staff to change an order, handle a modifier, split a bill and adjust a tip. Check what happens when the kitchen printer or internet connection fails. See Square vs Toast for a focused comparison.

Salons and appointment-based services: compare Vagaro

Vagaro combines appointment booking, staff calendars and business-management tools for beauty, wellness and fitness businesses. We would shortlist it when scheduling is central to the sale. Check the number of calendars and the cost of payment processing, messaging and any premium features in the quote.

Test a booking, cancellation, reschedule and package redemption. Confirm what clients receive and what staff can edit. A checkout demonstration alone will not show whether the calendar works for your team.

Complex retail inventory: include Lightspeed

Lightspeed Retail deserves a comparison when managing stock is a larger problem than taking payment. Demonstrate your actual variants, supplier orders and store transfers. Obtain a quote for the features and locations you need, including the payment-processing terms.

Compare total cost using your own sales

Calculate software, processing, hardware, add-ons and implementation separately. A $0.15 fixed charge on a $10 sale adds 1.5 percentage points before the percentage fee. On a $100 sale it adds 0.15 points. This arithmetic explains why two stores on the same rate can have different effective costs.

Ask each provider to price the same monthly sales volume, transaction count, card mix and number of locations. Also ask who owns the hardware and what happens to your data and contract if you leave. The POS pricing comparison and contract checklist can help organize those questions.
